input.content:
# DEVDESK-341 — Footer: replace the braille spinner by the shared activity dot

Status: plan, awaiting answer to one blocking question (§0). Author: architect.
Inputs: story summary (Plane not readable from this session), `docs/ux/footer-activity-indicator.md`,
user decisions Q1–Q4 (scope = router-driven sites only; progress in text only;
blurred = frozen `●`, no "(paused)"; no dot when the selected row's detail has a glyph).

## 0. Blocking question (to the user)

**The story's own example, `Updating from GitLab...`, is not a router-driven site.**
`internal/ui/forge/explorer/view.go:158` (`Loading <forge> <namespaces>...`) and `:163`
(`Updating from <forge>...`) take their frame from the explorer's own `spinner.Model`
(`explorer/update.go:268`). The explorer is one of the 8 `jobs.FrameMsg` consumers, but
the router frame it receives feeds no status of its own (its clone status has no
`Spinner`). Under Q1 as stated, that line keeps the braille spinner.

- **A — strict Q1.** The explorer only stops writing the router frame into its footer
  (step 2h). `Updating from GitLab...` stays braille until the follow-up story.
- **B — add the two explorer load lines** (step 7, +S). The explorer implements
  `WantsBlink()` while it loads, so the router's 500 ms chain runs. Its `spinner.Model`
  is deleted.
- Recommendation: **B**. It is the story's headline example, it costs little, and it
  also removes the explorer's two-writer race (below). Steps 1–6 do not depend on the
  answer.

## 1. Inventory (verified in code, commit 56166bf8)

### 1.1 The 8 router frame consumers (`m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)`)

| # | View | FrameMsg handler | Status site that shows the frame | What changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | dashboard | `dashboard/model.go:251` | `dashboard/view.go:299` `Spinner: true` (jobs line) | `Spinner` → `Activity` |
| b | `:jobs` | `jobsview/update.go:60` | `jobsview/view.go:121` `st.Spinner = …` | → `st.Activity` |
| c | ws | `workspaces/jobs.go:62` | `workspaces/view.go:167` | → `st.Activity` |
| d | templates | `templates/scan.go:229` | `templates/scan.go:272` | → `st.Activity` |
| e | `:sec` | `security/jobs.go:31` (only when `!spinnerAlive()`) | `security/view.go:209`, jobs half of the expression | split: `Spinner = inventoryLoading`, `Activity = !inventoryLoading && jobs…` |
| f | `:oci` | `oci_resources/jobs.go:61` (only when no tab load/search) | `oci_resources/view.go:124` | → `st.Activity`; lines 106/154/162 stay `Spinner` |
| g | `:files` | `filebrowser/jobs.go:42` | **none**: its status never sets `Spinner` (dead write) | remove the write |
| h | explorer | `forge/explorer/clone.go:211` | **none** of its own; it overwrites the frame of its own spinner (lines 158/163) on every router tick: two writers on one field | remove the write (§0 for the rest) |

So 6 status sites change what they render; g and h only lose the plumbing.

### 1.2 Out of scope (Q1): view-owned `spinner.Model` feeding a `Spinner: true` status

agent-usage (`view.go:282,298`), containers (`view.go:68`), netdiag (`header.go:280`,
`interfaces_model.go:354`), explorer (`view.go:158,163`, see §0), oci (`view.go:106,154,162`,
registry browser), security (`view.go:209` load half, `remediation.go:557,561`), viewer
(`view.go:75`). They keep `Status.Spinner` and `SetSpinnerFrame` unchanged.

Found along the way (for the follow-up story, not fixed here):
- **`:status`** (`status/view.go:127`, `Checking components...`, `Spinner: true`) runs a
  `spinner.Model` but never calls `SetSpinnerFrame`. The footer guard
  `f.spinnerFrame != ""` hides it: the spinner is invisible today, and its 10 Hz chain
  costs redraws for nothing.
- `setup` and `forge/auth` also own a `spinner.Model`, outside any footer. In `auth` it
  is `theme.SpinnerMessage` in the body.

## 2. Q5: do the view-owned spinners respect `app.motion: static` and the blur?

**No, neither.** Each runs its own `spinner.TickMsg` chain at `spinner.Dot.FPS` (10 Hz)
for as long as its `loading` flag holds, and stops only when the load ends.
- `motionStatic` is a router field (`App.motionStatic`). No view receives it, so no
  view spinner can honour it.
- Blur: `containers` and `agentusageview` handle `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`, but it only
  gates their data polls (`RefreshTickMsg`, `agentsResumeMsg`), never the spinner tick.
  The other five do not handle it at all.
- So during a load, a blurred terminal or `motion: static` still gets the 10 Hz
  braille. The cost is bounded by how long the load lasts, which is the argument for
  migrating them in the follow-up rather than adding motion/blur plumbing to 7 views.

## 3. Non-functional requirements

- **Cadence**: the footer dot's phase is the router's `jobs.FrameMsg.Blink` (1 Hz,
  500 ms half period, `blinkPhase`). A view starts no timer of its own for it (Rule 110).
  `motion: static` pins `●`. A blur (DEVDESK-210, `when_unfocused: pause`) pins `●`
  through the last frame the router already sends.
- **Layout**: the footer stays exactly one line of `width` columns, and the dot changes
  no height (Rule 124). The `●`/`○` swap must not move the text: both are one cell for
  `lipgloss.Width`, and both are East Asian *ambiguous*, so they can be two cells for
  `runewidth` (see risks).
- **Accessibility**: the text always says what is happening. The dot is redundant with
  it (shape plus colour, `ColorActivityRunning`). No new theme key (closed alias).
- **Precedence** is unchanged: error > warning > info > status. Progress stays in the
  text (`3/12`). No dot when `Detail.Glyph != ""` (Q4).
- **Cost**: no new chain. In-scope statuses are jobs-driven, and the router chain is
  alive whenever `Registry.Running()` (unfinished runs, all contexts) is > 0, which is a
  superset of every in-scope condition.

## 4. Options

| | A. `Status.Activity` + `FooterMessage.SetBlinkPhase` (recommended) | B. phase carried in `Status` (`Status{Activity, BlinkOn}`) | C. router renders the dot into `RenderedFrame` |
|---|---|---|---|
| View diff | `SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)` → `SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`; `Spinner` → `Activity` | each view stores `blink` in its model and copies it into every `Status` it builds | none in views |
| Mirrors existing pattern | yes: `table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` (Rule 125) | no: a render-time input duplicated in N status functions | no |
| Mixed views (sec, oci) | both writers disappear (no shared field) | same | **breaks**: the explorer and the mixed views alternate between braille and dot on the one field |
| Semantics | `Spinner` = view-owned load, `Activity` = jobs work; both explicit | same, more plumbing | `Spinner: true` means two things depending on who feeds the frame |
| Default without a call | dot steady `●` (zero value = on, like datatable) | must remember to copy | n/a |

**Recommendation: A.** It is the one with no hidden coupling: the view hands the
component the phase from the same handler that hands it to the table. C is the
smallest diff but keeps the ambiguity the story removes. B spreads one value across
every status function.

## 5. Interfaces (step 1)

```go
// internal/ui/components/footer_message.go

type Status struct {
	Text   string
	Detail RowDetail
	// Activity prefixes the shared activity dot (indicator.Running: ● or ○ on the
	// router's blink phase): work tracked by the jobs registry is in progress.
	// A detail with a glyph drops it (the row's own dot already says so).
	// When both Activity and Spinner are set, Activity wins.
	Activity bool
	// Spinner prepends the view-owned spinner frame: a table loading its rows.
	// Kept for the views DEVDESK-341 does not migrate (follow-up story).
	Spinner bool
	Level   Level
}

type FooterMessage struct {
	text         string
	level        Level
	id           uint64
	spinnerFrame string
	blinkOff     bool // zero value = "on": without SetBlinkPhase the dot is steady
}

// SetBlinkPhase stores the router's blink phase (jobs.FrameMsg.Blink) the
// activity dot renders with. Call it from Update(), in the view's
// jobs.FrameMsg handler (Rule 110).
func (f *FooterMessage) SetBlinkPhase(on bool)

// activityDot renders the Running glyph of the phase in its indicator colour on
// the app background (Rule 115). Unexported; the only place the footer builds it.
func activityDot(on bool) string // indicator.Style(indicator.Running).Background(theme.ColorBackground).Render(indicator.Glyph(indicator.Running, on))
```

Rendering in `View` (status branch only, timed messages untouched): the prefix is
`activityDot(!f.blinkOff) + theme.Bg(" ")` when `status.Activity && status.Detail.Glyph == ""`.
Otherwise it is the spinner frame, under the existing condition. The budget is reduced
by `lipgloss.Width(prefix)`. The East-Asian correction (`extra`) is computed over
`prefix + line` in **both** branches (Detail and plain text), not only the Detail one.
`components` already imports `internal/ui/indicator` (`job_activity.go`), so this adds
no import cycle.

## 6. Implementation plan

Conventions for every step: tests first (tester), then code (coder). Comments and
commit messages in English. Each step ends green on `go test` for the packages it
touches, `go vet` and `mise run lint`. Keys only through `internal/ui/testutil`.

### Step 1: `FooterMessage` learns the activity dot (S)

Files: `internal/ui/components/footer_message.go`, `footer_message_test.go`;
docs: `docs/architecture/ui-components.md` (§ "Le footer", usage block plus a paragraph
"Activity vs Spinner"), `.claude/rules/tui-behavior.md` Rule 128 (`Status` section:
`Activity` for jobs work, phase from `FrameMsg.Blink` via `SetBlinkPhase`; `Spinner`
kept for view-owned loads until the follow-up).

Tests (`footer_message_test.go`, section "The activity dot"):
1. `Status{Text:"1 job running", Activity:true}` with no `SetBlinkPhase` → stripped line contains `"● 1 job running"`.
2. `SetBlinkPhase(false)` → `"○ 1 job running"`. `SetBlinkPhase(true)` → `●`.
3. Raw SGR: the glyph carries the `ColorActivityRunning` foreground and the `ColorBackground` background (compare with `indicator.Style(indicator.Running)`). No `theme.SpinnerStyle` colour.
4. Same `Status`, phase on vs off → `lipgloss.Width` and `ansi.Strip` position of the text identical (no jitter).
5. `Activity:true` with `Detail{Glyph:"●", Lead:"Scanning ", Target:"x"}` → exactly one `●` in the line (Q4).
6. `Activity:true` with a `Detail` without a glyph → the dot is present.
7. `Activity:false` → no `●`/`○`, even after `SetBlinkPhase(false)`.
8. `f.Warn/Info/Error(...)` set → no dot, message text shown (precedence).
9. `Activity:true, Spinner:true` with `SetSpinnerFrame("⠹")` → dot present, no `⠹`.
10. Widths 1, 2, 3 → no panic, `lipgloss.Width(line) == width`. Width 2 with the dot → no overflow.
11. East Asian: `runewidth.DefaultCondition.EastAsianWidth = true` (restore in `t.Cleanup`, pattern of `datatable/indicator_eastasian_test.go`) → `theme.StringWidth(line) == width` for both phases.
12. Existing spinner tests (`TestALoadingStatusShowsTheSpinnerFrameThenTheText`, …) unchanged and green.

Command: `go test ./internal/ui/components`
Done when: all of the above pass. No view changed yet, and nothing on screen changes.

### Step 2: migrate the 8 router consumers (S each, **parallelizable 2a–2h after step 1**)

Common pattern for a, b, c, d: in `handleFrameMsg` (or the `case jobs.FrameMsg`),
replace `m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)` by
`m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`, and in the status function replace `Spinner` by
`Activity` (same condition). Rewrite the package's frame/footer tests that assert a
`RenderedFrame` placeholder (`"<R1>"`) in the footer.

Common tests per view (in the package's `frame_test.go` / `footer_test.go`):
- T1 jobs running, no glyph detail, `FrameMsg{Blink:true, RenderedFrame:"⠹"}` → footer contains `● ` + text, no `⠹`, no rune in U+2800–U+28FF.
- T2 then `FrameMsg{Blink:false}` → `○`, same text position.
- T3 snapshot with no unfinished run → no `●`/`○`.
- T4 a footer `Error` set while jobs run → error text, no dot.
- T5 (views with a row detail) selected row running with glyph detail → exactly one `●` (the detail's).
- T6 `FrameMsg` returns a nil Cmd (no view timer).

Status: plan, awaiting answer to one blocking question (§0). Author: architect.

## 0. Blocking question (to the user)

**The story's own example, `Updating from GitLab...`, is not a router-driven site.**
`internal/ui/forge/explorer/view.go:158` (`Loading <forge> <namespaces>...`) and `:163`
(`Updating from <forge>...`) take their frame from the explorer's own `spinner.Model`
(`explorer/update.go:268`). The explorer is one of the 8 `jobs.FrameMsg` consumers, but
the router frame it receives feeds no status of its own (its clone status has no
`Spinner`). Under Q1 as stated, that line keeps the braille spinner.

  (step 2h). `Updating from GitLab...` stays braille until the follow-up story.
- **B — add the two explorer load lines** (step 7, +S). The explorer implements
  `WantsBlink()` while it loads, so the router's 500 ms chain runs. Its `spinner.Model`
  is deleted.
- Recommendation: **B**. It is the story's headline example, it costs little, and it
  also removes the explorer's two-writer race (below). Steps 1–6 do not depend on the
  answer.

## 1. Inventory (verified in code, commit 56166bf8)

## 2. Q5: do the view-owned spinners respect `app.motion: static` and the blur?

**No, neither.** Each runs its own `spinner.TickMsg` chain at `spinner.Dot.FPS` (10 Hz)
for as long as its `loading` flag holds, and stops only when the load ends.
- `motionStatic` is a router field (`App.motionStatic`). No view receives it, so no
  view spinner can honour it.
- Blur: `containers` and `agentusageview` handle `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`, but it only
  gates their data polls (`RefreshTickMsg`, `agentsResumeMsg`), never the spinner tick.
  The other five do not handle it at all.
- So during a load, a blurred terminal or `motion: static` still gets the 10 Hz
  braille. The cost is bounded by how long the load lasts, which is the argument for
  migrating them in the follow-up rather than adding motion/blur plumbing to 7 views.

## 3. Non-functional requirements

- **Cadence**: the footer dot's phase is the router's `jobs.FrameMsg.Blink` (1 Hz,
  500 ms half period, `blinkPhase`). A view starts no timer of its own for it (Rule 110).
  `motion: static` pins `●`. A blur (DEVDESK-210, `when_unfocused: pause`) pins `●`
  through the last frame the router already sends.
- **Layout**: the footer stays exactly one line of `width` columns, and the dot changes
  no height (Rule 124). The `●`/`○` swap must not move the text: both are one cell for
  `lipgloss.Width`, and both are East Asian *ambiguous*, so they can be two cells for
  `runewidth` (see risks).
- **Accessibility**: the text always says what is happening. The dot is redundant with
  it (shape plus colour, `ColorActivityRunning`). No new theme key (closed alias).
- **Precedence** is unchanged: error > warning > info > status. Progress stays in the
  text (`3/12`). No dot when `Detail.Glyph != ""` (Q4).
- **Cost**: no new chain. In-scope statuses are jobs-driven, and the router chain is
  alive whenever `Registry.Running()` (unfinished runs, all contexts) is > 0, which is a
  superset of every in-scope condition.

## 4. Options

| | A. `Status.Activity` + `FooterMessage.SetBlinkPhase` (recommended) | B. phase carried in `Status` (`Status{Activity, BlinkOn}`) | C. router renders the dot into `RenderedFrame` |
|---|---|---|---|
| View diff | `SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)` → `SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`; `Spinner` → `Activity` | each view stores `blink` in its model and copies it into every `Status` it builds | none in views |
| Mirrors existing pattern | yes: `table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` (Rule 125) | no: a render-time input duplicated in N status functions | no |
| Mixed views (sec, oci) | both writers disappear (no shared field) | same | **breaks**: the explorer and the mixed views alternate between braille and dot on the one field |
| Semantics | `Spinner` = view-owned load, `Activity` = jobs work; both explicit | same, more plumbing | `Spinner: true` means two things depending on who feeds the frame |
| Default without a call | dot steady `●` (zero value = on, like datatable) | must remember to copy | n/a |

**Recommendation: A.** It is the one with no hidden coupling: the view hands the
component the phase from the same handler that hands it to the table. C is the
smallest diff but keeps the ambiguity the story removes. B spreads one value across
every status function.

| **Total** | **M** (steps 1–6), **M+** with step 7 | no new dependency, no design unknown left besides §0 |

cleanup), 341c = step 7 or the follow-up for the 7 view-owned spinners plus `:status`.

# DEVDESK-341 — Footer: replace the braille spinner by the shared activity dot

Status: plan, awaiting answer to one blocking question (§0). Author: architect.
Inputs: story summary (Plane not readable from this session), `docs/ux/footer-activity-indicator.md`,
user decisions Q1–Q4 (scope = router-driven sites only; progress in text only;
blurred = frozen `●`, no "(paused)"; no dot when the selected row's detail has a glyph).

## 0. Blocking question (to the user)

**The story's own example, `Updating from GitLab...`, is not a router-driven site.**
`internal/ui/forge/explorer/view.go:158` (`Loading <forge> <namespaces>...`) and `:163`
(`Updating from <forge>...`) take their frame from the explorer's own `spinner.Model`
(`explorer/update.go:268`). The explorer is one of the 8 `jobs.FrameMsg` consumers, but
the router frame it receives feeds no status of its own (its clone status has no
`Spinner`). Under Q1 as stated, that line keeps the braille spinner.

- **A — strict Q1.** The explorer only stops writing the router frame into its footer
  (step 2h). `Updating from GitLab...` stays braille until the follow-up story.
- **B — add the two explorer load lines** (step 7, +S). The explorer implements
  `WantsBlink()` while it loads, so the router's 500 ms chain runs. Its `spinner.Model`
  is deleted.
- Recommendation: **B**. It is the story's headline example, it costs little, and it
  also removes the explorer's two-writer race (below). Steps 1–6 do not depend on the
  answer.

## 1. Inventory (verified in code, commit 56166bf8)

### 1.1 The 8 router frame consumers (`m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)`)

| # | View | FrameMsg handler | Status site that shows the frame | What changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | dashboard | `dashboard/model.go:251` | `dashboard/view.go:299` `Spinner: true` (jobs line) | `Spinner` → `Activity` |
| b | `:jobs` | `jobsview/update.go:60` | `jobsview/view.go:121` `st.Spinner = …` | → `st.Activity` |
| c | ws | `workspaces/jobs.go:62` | `workspaces/view.go:167` | → `st.Activity` |
| d | templates | `templates/scan.go:229` | `templates/scan.go:272` | → `st.Activity` |
| e | `:sec` | `security/jobs.go:31` (only when `!spinnerAlive()`) | `security/view.go:209`, jobs half of the expression | split: `Spinner = inventoryLoading`, `Activity = !inventoryLoading && jobs…` |
| f | `:oci` | `oci_resources/jobs.go:61` (only when no tab load/search) | `oci_resources/view.go:124` | → `st.Activity`; lines 106/154/162 stay `Spinner` |
| g | `:files` | `filebrowser/jobs.go:42` | **none**: its status never sets `Spinner` (dead write) | remove the write |
| h | explorer | `forge/explorer/clone.go:211` | **none** of its own; it overwrites the frame of its own spinner (lines 158/163) on every router tick: two writers on one field | remove the write (§0 for the rest) |

So 6 status sites change what they render; g and h only lose the plumbing.

### 1.2 Out of scope (Q1): view-owned `spinner.Model` feeding a `Spinner: true` status

agent-usage (`view.go:282,298`), containers (`view.go:68`), netdiag (`header.go:280`,
`interfaces_model.go:354`), explorer (`view.go:158,163`, see §0), oci (`view.go:106,154,162`,
registry browser), security (`view.go:209` load half, `remediation.go:557,561`), viewer
(`view.go:75`). They keep `Status.Spinner` and `SetSpinnerFrame` unchanged.

Found along the way (for the follow-up story, not fixed here):
- **`:status`** (`status/view.go:127`, `Checking components...`, `Spinner: true`) runs a
  `spinner.Model` but never calls `SetSpinnerFrame`. The footer guard
  `f.spinnerFrame != ""` hides it: the spinner is invisible today, and its 10 Hz chain
  costs redraws for nothing.
- `setup` and `forge/auth` also own a `spinner.Model`, outside any footer. In `auth` it
  is `theme.SpinnerMessage` in the body.

## 2. Q5: do the view-owned spinners respect `app.motion: static` and the blur?

**No, neither.** Each runs its own `spinner.TickMsg` chain at `spinner.Dot.FPS` (10 Hz)
for as long as its `loading` flag holds, and stops only when the load ends.
- `motionStatic` is a router field (`App.motionStatic`). No view receives it, so no
  view spinner can honour it.
- Blur: `containers` and `agentusageview` handle `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`, but it only
  gates their data polls (`RefreshTickMsg`, `agentsResumeMsg`), never the spinner tick.
  The other five do not handle it at all.
- So during a load, a blurred terminal or `motion: static` still gets the 10 Hz
  braille. The cost is bounded by how long the load lasts, which is the argument for
  migrating them in the follow-up rather than adding motion/blur plumbing to 7 views.

## 3. Non-functional requirements

- **Cadence**: the footer dot's phase is the router's `jobs.FrameMsg.Blink` (1 Hz,
  500 ms half period, `blinkPhase`). A view starts no timer of its own for it (Rule 110).
  `motion: static` pins `●`. A blur (DEVDESK-210, `when_unfocused: pause`) pins `●`
  through the last frame the router already sends.
- **Layout**: the footer stays exactly one line of `width` columns, and the dot changes
  no height (Rule 124). The `●`/`○` swap must not move the text: both are one cell for
  `lipgloss.Width`, and both are East Asian *ambiguous*, so they can be two cells for
  `runewidth` (see risks).
- **Accessibility**: the text always says what is happening. The dot is redundant with
  it (shape plus colour, `ColorActivityRunning`). No new theme key (closed alias).
- **Precedence** is unchanged: error > warning > info > status. Progress stays in the
  text (`3/12`). No dot when `Detail.Glyph != ""` (Q4).
- **Cost**: no new chain. In-scope statuses are jobs-driven, and the router chain is
  alive whenever `Registry.Running()` (unfinished runs, all contexts) is > 0, which is a
  superset of every in-scope condition.

## 4. Options

| | A. `Status.Activity` + `FooterMessage.SetBlinkPhase` (recommended) | B. phase carried in `Status` (`Status{Activity, BlinkOn}`) | C. router renders the dot into `RenderedFrame` |
|---|---|---|---|
| View diff | `SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)` → `SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`; `Spinner` → `Activity` | each view stores `blink` in its model and copies it into every `Status` it builds | none in views |
| Mirrors existing pattern | yes: `table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` (Rule 125) | no: a render-time input duplicated in N status functions | no |
| Mixed views (sec, oci) | both writers disappear (no shared field) | same | **breaks**: the explorer and the mixed views alternate between braille and dot on the one field |
| Semantics | `Spinner` = view-owned load, `Activity` = jobs work; both explicit | same, more plumbing | `Spinner: true` means two things depending on who feeds the frame |
| Default without a call | dot steady `●` (zero value = on, like datatable) | must remember to copy | n/a |

**Recommendation: A.** It is the one with no hidden coupling: the view hands the
component the phase from the same handler that hands it to the table. C is the
smallest diff but keeps the ambiguity the story removes. B spreads one value across
every status function.

## 5. Interfaces (step 1)

```go
// internal/ui/components/footer_message.go

type Status struct {
	Text   string
	Detail RowDetail
	// Activity prefixes the shared activity dot (indicator.Running: ● or ○ on the
	// router's blink phase): work tracked by the jobs registry is in progress.
	// A detail with a glyph drops it (the row's own dot already says so).
	// When both Activity and Spinner are set, Activity wins.
	Activity bool
	// Spinner prepends the view-owned spinner frame: a table loading its rows.
	// Kept for the views DEVDESK-341 does not migrate (follow-up story).
	Spinner bool
	Level   Level
}

type FooterMessage struct {
	text         string
	level        Level
	id           uint64
	spinnerFrame string
	blinkOff     bool // zero value = "on": without SetBlinkPhase the dot is steady
}

// SetBlinkPhase stores the router's blink phase (jobs.FrameMsg.Blink) the
// activity dot renders with. Call it from Update(), in the view's
// jobs.FrameMsg handler (Rule 110).
func (f *FooterMessage) SetBlinkPhase(on bool)

// activityDot renders the Running glyph of the phase in its indicator colour on
// the app background (Rule 115). Unexported; the only place the footer builds it.
func activityDot(on bool) string // indicator.Style(indicator.Running).Background(theme.ColorBackground).Render(indicator.Glyph(indicator.Running, on))
```

  - "A row dot or a loading spinner": three rows (row dot / **footer activity dot**: jobs work in the view, `Status.Activity`, phase from `FrameMsg.Blink` / loading spinner: view-owned, out of scope, list the 7). The "own spinner is not the router's chain" sentence states Q5 (no motion, no blur).
  - Cadence table: the line "footer spinners depend on the frame" is updated by step 5.
- `docs/architecture/ui-components.md`: "The selected row in the footer": "A detail with a glyph suppresses the spinner **or the activity dot**".
- `.claude/rules/tui-tables.md` Rule 139 (loading text unchanged; jobs progress is `Activity`), Rule 125 (activity column: the footer dot shares the alphabet and the phase).
- `docs-site/docs/explanation/ui-components.md` and `app-shell.md` (mirrors): same changes (techwriter).
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/backlog.md`: note the follow-up story (7 view-owned spinners, the invisible `:status` spinner).

Done when: no doc still says the router frame feeds a footer.
Check: `grep -rn 'RenderedFrame\|SetSpinnerFrame' docs .claude/rules docs-site/docs`
only lists the out-of-scope spinner usage.

### Step 5: retire the braille frame from the router (S–M, optional, separable)

Hypothesis: included in this story as a separate commit. Once step 2 is done nothing
reads `FrameMsg.Frame` or `RenderedFrame`. The router still advances a braille index
and runs at 100 ms while jobs run, for no consumer. Without this step the app keeps a
10 Hz chain during every job. It can be moved to the follow-up without affecting
steps 1–4.

Files: `internal/jobs/message.go` (remove `Frame`, `RenderedFrame`),
`internal/jobs/frame_test.go`, `internal/app/animation.go` (remove `frameIdx`,
`animationFrame`, `animationFastInterval`, the `spinner` import; `frameMsg()` returns
`FrameMsg{Blink: a.anim.blinkOn}`), `animation_test.go`, `animation_chain_test.go`,
`animation_router_test.go`, `redraw_measure_test.go`, `app-shell.md` cadence table.

New cadence (prudent variant):

```go
// cadence returns the chain interval, false when nothing needs one. Running work
// keeps a 500 ms chain even under static motion so time-based text (Started,
// Duration) still refreshes; a blink alone does not run under static motion.
func cadence(running, wantsBlink, static bool) (time.Duration, bool)
```

| running | wantsBlink | static | → |
|---|---|---|---|
| true | any | any | 500 ms, true |
| false | true | false | 500 ms, true |
| false | true | true | 0, false |
| false | false | any | 0, false |

Tests: the table above (`TestCadence…`). Phase still alternates strictly at 500 ms
under `tea.Every`. One chain only (`TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain` unchanged).
Blur → no chain (unchanged). `TestTheAnimationChainUnderARealProgram` under `-race`.
The jobs field-shape test now expects `{Blink}` only.

Commands: `go test ./internal/jobs ./internal/app`,
`CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./internal/app -run Animation`, then `mise run check`.
Done when: the build has no `spinner` import in `internal/app/animation.go`, and every
test is green.

### Step 6: final check (XS)

`mise run check`, `mise run test-race`, then a manual run (`mise run dev`):
ws `F` sync on several repos with the cursor on an idle row → blinking `●`/`○` + text.
Same with `app.motion: static` → steady `●`. Blur the terminal → frozen `●`. Sync done
→ dot gone. Error during sync → red text, no dot.

### Step 7: only if §0 is answered B: explorer loads on the shared dot (S)

Files: `forge/explorer/model.go`, `update.go`, `view.go`, `index.go`, `navigation.go`,
`clone.go`, new `activity.go` or added to `jobs.go`, tests `frame_test.go`,
`footer_test.go`, `index_test.go`, plus `explorer_activity_test.go` in `internal/app`.
- `func (m Model) WantsBlink() bool { return m.loadingTree() || m.refreshing > 0 }` (the router's `BlinkingView`).
- `handleFrameMsg` adds `m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`. `view.go:158,163` → `Activity: true`.
- Delete the explorer's `spinner.Model`, `handleSpinnerTick`, the `spinner.TickMsg` case and the `m.spinner.Tick` batches.
- Tests: refreshing → `● Updating from GitLab...`, phase off → `○`. Load done → no dot, and `WantsBlink()` false. Router: explorer refreshing, no job → chain at 500 ms. Static → no chain, `●`. Activity guard: add the explorer to `footerActivitySeeds`, and its package to the `spinner.Model`-free list if step 3 adds one.

Command: `go test ./internal/ui/forge/explorer ./internal/app -run 'Explorer|ActivityGuard'`.

## 7. Order and parallelism

```
1 ──► 2a 2b 2c 2d 2e 2f 2g 2h (parallel) ──► 3 ──► 4 ─┐
                                              └──► 5 ─┴──► 6
7 (if B): after 1 and 2h, in parallel with 3–5 (then add its seed to 3)
```

## 8. Risks and irreversible points

- **Same glyph, two meanings**: the footer dot and a running row's detail are both `●`. The existing footer guard only checks presence, so it would pass on a double dot. Mitigated by step 3.2 (exactly one).
- **East Asian ambiguous width** (`●`, `○`): `lipgloss.Width` = 1 and `runewidth` = 2 under `EastAsianWidth`. The spinner (braille) never had this problem. Without the correction, the line is one column too wide and wraps (Rule 124). Mitigated by step 1, test 11.
- **Two alphabets inside one view until the follow-up**: sec and oci show braille for their own loads and the dot for jobs. The explorer too, unless §0 is answered B. Accepted by Q1; to be stated in the PR.
- **Dot shown without a live chain**: impossible for the in-scope sites, which are all jobs-driven: `Registry.Running()` counts every unfinished run in every context, a superset of every view's condition. A future `Activity` status that does not depend on jobs must implement `WantsBlink()`, otherwise it shows a steady `●` (harmless, but no blink). Write this in Rule 128.
- **Frozen `●` when blurred** looks like a hang (Q3 accepted). The text stays truthful.
- **Step 5** changes the router's cadence (100 → 500 ms while jobs run). Time-based text refreshes less often: at most 0.5 s late, and still refreshed under static motion with the prudent variant. Tests that assert 100 ms must be rewritten, not deleted.
- **Irreversible**: none. Everything is internal (no config key, no file format, no theme key). Removing `FrameMsg.Frame/RenderedFrame` (step 5) is an internal API break, compile-checked.

## 9. Effort (re-estimate)

| Part | Effort | Assumption |
|---|---|---|
| Step 1 | S | ~40 lines plus 11 table tests; reuses `indicator`, the `extra` correction exists |
| Step 2 (8 sub-steps) | S each, M total | 1–5 production lines per view; most of the time goes into rewriting ~30 test assertions that check a `RenderedFrame` placeholder |
| Step 3 | S–M | 6 new seeds, of which ws/templates/sec/oci exist as patterns; positive-injection check |
| Step 4 | S | 6 doc files, 2 of them mirrors |
| Step 5 | S–M | router tests on cadence and chain under `-race` |
| Step 7 (if B) | S | delete a spinner and add `WantsBlink` |
| **Total** | **M** (steps 1–6), **M+** with step 7 | no new dependency, no design unknown left besides §0 |

Story split if needed: 341a = steps 1–4 (visible change), 341b = step 5 (router
cleanup), 341c = step 7 or the follow-up for the 7 view-owned spinners plus `:status`.

input.message:
Le plan est écrit dans `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.claude/plans/DEVDESK-341-plan.md`. Je n'ai modifié aucun autre fichier. Je n'ai pas pu lire la story dans Plane (pas d'outil Plane dans cette session) : je me suis appuyé sur ton résumé et sur l'avis UX.

## Question bloquante (à poser à l'utilisateur)
L'exemple central de la story, « Updating from GitLab... », sort du périmètre Q1 tel qu'il est formulé. Ce texte (`forge/explorer/view.go:163`, de même que `:158` « Loading … ») prend son image dans le `spinner.Model` propre à l'explorer, pas dans le tick du routeur.
- **A** : appliquer Q1 strictement. Cette ligne reste en braille jusqu'à la story de suivi.
- **B** : migrer aussi ces deux lignes de chargement (étape 7, effort S). L'explorer implémente `WantsBlink()` pendant le chargement et son `spinner.Model` est supprimé.
- Ma recommandation : **B**. Les étapes 1 à 6 n'en dépendent pas.

## Inventaire (vérifié dans le code)
- **8 vues consomment `jobs.FrameMsg.RenderedFrame`** : dashboard, jobsview, workspaces, templates, security, oci, filebrowser, explorer.
- **6 seulement l'affichent réellement** dans leur footer, et c'est là que l'apparence change :
  - `dashboard/view.go:299`, `jobsview/view.go:121`, `workspaces/view.go:167`, `templates/scan.go:272` ;
  - `security/view.go:209`, partie jobs seulement ;
  - `oci_resources/view.go:124`.
- **filebrowser** reçoit l'image du routeur, mais aucun statut n'active `Spinner` : l'écriture ne sert à rien.
- **explorer** écrase avec l'image du routeur celle de son propre spinner : deux écritures concurrentes sur le même champ.
- **Hors sujet, mais à reprendre dans la story de suivi** : `:status` fait tourner un `spinner.Model` sans jamais appeler `SetSpinnerFrame`. Son spinner est invisible et son chaînage à 10 Hz ne sert à rien.

## Option retenue
J'ai comparé trois options :
- A : `Status.Activity` + `FooterMessage.SetBlinkPhase(on bool)`, sur le modèle de `table.SetBlinkPhase` ;
- B : la phase transportée dans `Status` ;
- C : le routeur dessine directement la pastille dans `RenderedFrame`.

Je recommande **A**. C produit le plus petit diff, mais dans les vues mixtes (et dans l'explorer, qui ne protège pas le champ) la même ligne alternerait entre braille et pastille. `Spinner` + `SetSpinnerFrame` restent en place pour les 7 spinners hors périmètre.

## Étapes
1. Dans `FooterMessage`, ajout de `Status.Activity` et `SetBlinkPhase`. La pastille ●/○ prend `indicator.Style(Running)` sur le fond de l'application ; il n'y a pas de pastille quand `Detail.Glyph` est présent ; `Activity` l'emporte sur `Spinner` ; la correction de largeur Est-asiatique s'applique ; 11 tests. (S)
2. Migration des 8 vues consommatrices, en parallèle de 2a à 2h. On remplace `SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)` par `SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` et `Spinner` par `Activity`. Security et oci se séparent entre « chargement » (braille) et « jobs » (pastille), et leurs gardes anti-double-écriture disparaissent. Filebrowser et explorer perdent seulement l'écriture. (S chacune)
3. Gardes :
   - aucun braille (U+2800–U+28FF) dans le footer des vues migrées, avec une image de routeur non vide forcée pour que le test morde ;
   - exactement un ● quand la ligne sélectionnée a une pastille ;
   - `RenderedFrame` interdit sous `internal/ui` ;
   - tests d'acceptation au niveau du routeur : phase on puis off, `motion: static` donne ● fixe, perte du focus donne ● figé, fin du job fait disparaître la pastille, une erreur l'emporte ;
   - chaque garde est vérifiée en réinjectant l'ancien code. (S–M)
4. Documentation : Rule 128, 125 et 139, `app-shell.md`, `ui-components.md`, les copies dans `docs-site`, et une note dans `backlog.md`. (S)
5. Facultative et séparable (hypothèse : incluse, en commit à part) : retrait de `FrameMsg.Frame`/`RenderedFrame` et de la cadence à 100 ms. Le routeur passe à 500 ms tant que des jobs tournent, y compris en `static`, pour que les durées affichées continuent de se rafraîchir. (S–M)
6. Vérification finale : `mise run check`, `mise run test-race`, puis un essai manuel (sync ws, `static`, perte du focus, erreur). (XS)
7. Seulement si B : chargements de l'explorer sur la pastille partagée. (S)

Ordre : 1, puis 2a–2h en parallèle, puis 3, puis 4 et 5, puis 6. L'étape 7 peut se faire en parallèle à partir de l'étape 2h.

## Réponse à Q5
**Non, ni l'un ni l'autre.** Les 7 `spinner.Model` propres aux vues tournent à 10 Hz tant que leur indicateur `loading` reste vrai, et s'arrêtent seulement à la fin du chargement.
- `motionStatic` n'existe que dans le routeur : aucune vue ne le reçoit.
- containers et agent-usage reçoivent `TerminalFocusMsg`, mais s'en servent seulement pour suspendre leurs relectures de données, jamais pour arrêter le spinner. Les 5 autres ne le traitent pas du tout.

Le coût reste limité à la durée du chargement : c'est un argument pour les migrer dans la story de suivi plutôt que d'ajouter la gestion du focus et du mode `static` dans 7 vues.

## Risques
- ● sert à la fois de pastille du footer et de pastille de la ligne sélectionnée : la garde actuelle passerait avec deux ●. Couvert par l'étape 3.2.
- ●/○ ont une largeur Est-asiatique ambiguë, ce qui peut faire déborder la ligne d'une colonne. Couvert par le test 11 de l'étape 1.
- Deux alphabets cohabitent temporairement dans sec, oci et l'explorer.
- Une future valeur `Activity` qui ne dépend pas des jobs devra implémenter `WantsBlink()`, sinon la pastille reste fixe. À écrire dans la Rule 128.
- L'étape 5 modifie la cadence du routeur : des tests sont à réécrire.
- Aucun point irréversible : tout est interne, sans clé de configuration ni de thème.

## Effort réestimé
**M** pour les étapes 1 à 6, **M+** avec l'étape 7. L'essentiel du temps passe dans la réécriture d'environ 30 assertions de test qui vérifient un `RenderedFrame` factice. Si l'effort doit être découpé : 341a = étapes 1–4, 341b = étape 5, 341c = étape 7 ou la story de suivi.
